title: CorDBA: Corners Decoupled Bayesian Approach for yield optimization
problem: Yield optimization for advanced nodes is challenging due to limited resources and high cost of transistor-level simulation in yield estimation.
motivation: Process variations create complex yield-performance relationships; simulations are expensive at advanced nodes, limiting optimization iterations.
method: CorDBA avoids expensive transistor-level simulations by separating yield improvement from yield measurement. It uses statistical process-variation corners (predicted worst-case manufacturing scenarios) to identify where circuits might fail. Then it optimizes using max-minimum optimization, which focuses on making even the worst-performing chips as robust as possible. This multi-stage approach lets designers refine designs without constantly re-running expensive simulations.
key_novelty: The key idea is decoupling—improving yield without expensive simulations by using statistical process predictions and optimizing for the worst-performing chips.
limitations: Evaluated on analog, digital, and emerging devices but lacks large-scale integration design results.
primary_theme: Efficient yield optimization via decoupled corner-based approach
